gap: No result ChatGPT got says how many watts the laptop gets while a phone charges from the same brick for the two chargers it recommended. The $35.99 Anker Nano 100W (A2679) has only one port, so the answer is none. Anker gives the Prime 100W (A2688) only as a 100 W two-port total, and anker.com now lists it as sold out. At the same $69.99, Anker's Prime 200W (A2683) gives the laptop 100 W with a phone plugged in: $0.70 per laptop watt, against $0.90 for the 140W 4-port (A2697).
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT got: Anker A120F (ranks 1, 3 and 4), A2688 (ranks 2, 7 and 12) and A121B (ranks 5 and 8), plus Anker's 'for laptops' collection, which ChatGPT got as rank 10. The A2688 page gives only totals ('Two Ports in Use: 100W Max', 'Three Ports in Use: 89W Max'), not the laptop port's share. The A120F page is a single-port charger. The A121B page does give a split (70W + 30W, or 67W + 33W), but anker.com shows it as sold out. None of these pages works out watts per dollar for the laptop port while a second device charges, or watts per ounce. ChatGPT's answer did not mention that its Nano 100W pick has one port or that its Prime 100W pick is out of stock at Anker US.
decides: It changes the pick. For 'laptop plus phone from one brick', ChatGPT's $35.99 Nano 100W cannot do it because it has one port. Its $69.99 Prime 100W is sold out on anker.com, and Anker states no laptop-port wattage for it when two ports are in use. For the same $69.99, the Prime 200W (A2683) keeps 100 W on the laptop port with a phone on a second USB-C port ($0.70 per laptop watt). It is a 563 g desktop brick, though: 10.1 W/oz against 23.6 W/oz for the Nano. So for travel with one device, the Nano 100W stays the best value at $0.36 per watt. For a desk with a laptop and a phone, the Prime 200W wins on price per laptop watt. Our current page's Anker row ('See maker page; sold on Amazon') should say sold out at Anker US as of 2026-11-17.
